SUPERSEDES this chapter's first 'pdf' manifest entry, which used a plain page.get_text() string and found 5 'missing' numbers (ex_8.2's '11', q_8.1's '9', q_8.6's '9') - a FALSE positive, not a real content gap. Root cause: this chapter's stage 9 converter renders exponents as HTML <sup>...</sup> spans holding ordinary ASCII digits (not literal unicode superscript glyphs like the '10³⁹' case step_10/PROMPT.md documents) - page.get_text() concatenates a <sup> span's text directly against its neighbour with no separator, so '10' immediately followed by an exponent span '11' merges into one token '1011', hiding both '10' and '11' from ever matching standalone. This is the SAME class of bug the documented unicode-superscript trap describes (a base number gluing to its own exponent), just manifesting through a different technical mechanism (HTML <sup> + font-size shrink, not special superscript codepoints) - worth recording here since a future chapter reusing yet another rendering technique for exponents could hit a third variant of the same underlying problem. Fixed by extracting text via page.get_text('dict') and inserting a separating space between consecutive spans on the same line whenever their font size differs by more than 0.3pt (a real, measurable per-span signal fitz exposes, confirmed empirically: a <sup> span's size is reliably smaller than its neighbours', e.g. 9.92pt body text vs 8.27pt/6.89pt exponents) - '10' and its exponent now extract as two distinct tokens.
